key_insight: Oncology-specific language models and tokenizers better capture real-world outpatient cancer notes than general adjacent-domain encoders.
clinical_relevance: For oncology NLP tasks, adapting both the model and the tokenizer to local note style may improve representation quality before downstream use.
method: Compared RadBERT and PathologyBERT against two local models: continued pretraining (OncoNote-RadBERT) and training from scratch (OncoNoteBERT).
Used 290,026 outpatient oncology notes from 21,564 UK patients with lung or head-and-neck cancer.
Evaluated perplexity, masked-language modelling, token fragmentation, clinical term tokenisation, and masked-token probes.
evidence_signal: OncoNote-RadBERT had the best corpus fit (perplexity 2.10), while OncoNoteBERT had more efficient tokenisation and acceptable masked-token predictions for 12/13 probes.
watch_item: Better perplexity did not always mean better token-level clinical predictions, so tokenizer fragmentation and local validation need careful review before deployment.
paper_title: OncoNoteBERT: A Foundation Representation Model for Natural Language Processing of Real-World Outpatient Oncology Notes
